message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | Key Rights | How to Exercise Them | |------|------------|----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any receipts for repairs.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if you disagree. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, etc.).
• Must comply with all building, health, and safety codes. | • Report problems in writing (email or letter).
• If unresolved, you may file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or local code enforcement. | | **Rent Payment & Late Fees** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Landlord may charge a late fee only if it’s stated in the lease and is reasonable (usually not more than 5% of the monthly rent). | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if needed.
• Keep records of all payments. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a month‑to‑month lease with **30 days’ written notice**.
• For fixed‑term leases, the landlord must give notice before the lease expires if they intend not to renew. | • Provide written notice (email or letter) and keep a copy. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Report disturbances; if persistent, seek mediation or legal action. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24–48 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of entries; if you suspect unlawful entry, consult an attorney. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or TDHCA. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but only after giving written notice and a reasonable deadline. | • Document the problem, send notice, keep receipts, and calculate the deduction carefully. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the Texas eviction procedure: serve a **Notice to Pay Rent or Quit** (10 days) or **Notice to Vacate** (30 days) for non‑payment or lease violations.
• Eviction must be filed in court; the landlord cannot forcibly remove you. | • Respond promptly to notices; consider mediation or legal counsel. | | **Fair Housing** | • Texas law protects against discrimination in housing. | • Report violations to HUD or TDHCA. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide essential utilities unless otherwise agreed. | • Verify utility responsibilities in the lease. | | **Insurance** | • Landlord is not required to provide renter’s insurance, but you may obtain it for personal protection. | • Consider renter’s insurance for belongings and liability. | #### Practical Steps for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Understand all terms, especially those about deposits, maintenance, and notice periods. 2. **Keep Written Records** – Emails, texts, and written notices help protect your rights. 3. **Know the Local Ordinances** – Some cities in Texas have additional tenant protections (e.g., rent control, eviction moratoriums). 4. **Seek Legal Advice** – If you face disputes, consult a Texas attorney or a tenant advocacy group (e.g., Texas Tenants Union). 5. **Use Official Channels** – File complaints with TDHCA, HUD, or local code enforcement when necessary. --- **Disclaimer:** This overview is for informational purposes only and does not constitute legal advice. Laws can change, and local ordinances may add additional protections. For specific legal questions, consult a licensed attorney in Texas.
